title: Binary Tree Preorder Traversal
statement:
You are given the root of a binary tree. Return the values of its nodes in **preorder**: a node is visited first, then every node of its left subtree, then every node of its right subtree.

The tree can be a very long chain of nodes, so a solution that recurses once per node may run out of stack space. Interviewers at several companies specifically ask for the version that uses an explicit stack instead of recursion.

**Follow-up:** Solve it iteratively with an explicit stack, then discuss how Morris traversal reaches `O(1)` extra space.
inputFormat: A single line with the level-order serialization of the tree: node values separated by spaces, with `null` for a missing child. The root comes first, then the children of each node level by level from left to right. Children of a `null` entry are not listed, and trailing `null` entries are omitted.
outputFormat: Print the preorder values on one line, separated by single spaces.
constraints: The tree may have height up to 10^5

examples.explanation: The root 1 is visited first. Then its left subtree is traversed completely: 2, then 4, then 5. Finally the right subtree, which is just 3.
Node 8 has only a right child 6. Node 6 has a left child 5, and 5 has a right child 7 (the single `null` after 5 is its missing left child). Preorder visits 8, 6, 5, 7.
A single node is its own traversal.

complexity.space: O(h) for the explicit stack, where h is the tree height

hints: Preorder means the node is processed before either child. What data structure naturally reverses the order in which you push things?
Push the root. Repeatedly pop a node, record it, then push its right child before its left child so that the left child is popped first.
A chain of 10^5 nodes would overflow a recursive solution in many languages, which is why the stack is explicit.
